Inputs: layered keyframes; JavaScript-based expressions binding properties
Inference_Locus: Composition resolves from layered keyframes and expressions, procedural bindings evaluated deterministically per frame. Working state stays addressable.
Date_Note: Compositing and animation core per Wikipedia.
Notes: Procedural dependencies place it near Houdini SOP on the x axis.

Inputs: Bezier paths, anchor points, appearance attributes, effect parameters
Inference_Locus: Artwork resolves from Bezier paths and appearance attributes the designer sets; geometry stays addressable at anchor-point level and rendering is deterministic.
Date_Note: Vector core since the 1987 original per Wikipedia.

Inputs: layer stack, masks, blend modes, adjustment parameters set directly
Inference_Locus: The composite resolves from the layer stack: pixel and adjustment layers, masks, and blend modes the designer sets directly. Rendering is deterministic and edits stay addressable as working state.
Date_Note: Layers introduced in Photoshop 3.0 (1994) per Wikipedia.
Notes: Seed anchor row (8.5/2.0).

Inputs: clip in/out points, track arrangement, transitions, effect parameters, keyframes
Inference_Locus: The program resolves from the sequence: clips, cuts, transitions, and effect parameters placed on the timeline. Rendering is deterministic and edit decisions stay addressable.
Date_Note: Timeline-based NLE core per Wikipedia.

Inputs: layer and generator stacks; baked mesh maps (curvature, ambient occlusion); exposed parameters
Inference_Locus: Materials resolve procedurally from layer stacks and generators reading baked mesh maps such as curvature and ambient occlusion, placing effects by rule: wear on edges, dirt in cavities. Deterministic and re-editable.
Date_Note: Long-standing Painter capability; not dated in source.
Notes: Adaptivity is procedural, driven by baked data rather than learned structure.

Inputs: an uploaded spoken-audio recording; a strength slider
Inference_Locus: A model resolves cleaned speech from an uploaded recording, attenuating background noise, reverb, and music; a strength slider balances processed against original audio. Runs as a hosted web service.
Date_Note: v2 current on podcast.adobe.com; v2 announcement date to be confirmed.
Notes: Free tier processes files under 30 minutes per coverage.

Inputs: a mask over the region to remove across frames; optional hand-edited reference frame
Inference_Locus: Resolves fill for a masked region across footage from surrounding spatial and temporal content; a hand-edited reference frame can condition the fill. Invoked per masked span from the Content-Aware Fill panel.
Date_Note: Documented in current AE help; ship date not stated in source.

Inputs: brush strokes on a base frame; corrective strokes on subsequent frames
Inference_Locus: A segmentation model resolves a subject matte from brush strokes on one frame and propagates it across footage frame by frame; corrective strokes recondition the propagation. Suited to hair, overlapping limbs, and transparency per Adobe's documentation.
Model_Backend: proprietary (new model in Next-Gen Roto Brush)
Date_Note: Next-Gen Roto Brush (3.0) documented in current AE help; ship date to be confirmed.
Notes: Temporal propagation gives it higher recurrence than still-image masking.

Inputs: selected vector artwork plus a text prompt describing palette or mood
Inference_Locus: A model resolves a recoloring of selected vector artwork from a text prompt; geometry is unchanged and colors are remapped. Invoked from the Recolor workflow with variations to pick from.
Date_Note: Beta June 2023; in Illustrator 27.9, September 2023.
Notes: Inference is confined to the palette; structure is fully designer-governed.

Inputs: the photo; choice of mask type; parametric adjustments applied through the mask
Inference_Locus: Segmentation models resolve subject or sky masks from the photo inside the redesigned masking panel; adjustments applied through the mask stay parametric and re-editable, and masks can be inverted or combined.
Date_Note: October 2021: Lightroom 11, Lightroom Classic 11, Camera Raw 14.
Notes: Later releases added people and object masking; held provisionally.

Inputs: a Bayer or X-Trans raw file plus one amount slider
Inference_Locus: A model resolves a demosaiced, noise-reduced DNG from raw sensor data with a single amount control; output stacks alongside the original. Runs per image on desktop.
Date_Note: April 2023 Lightroom releases.
Notes: Source notes raw-mosaic support and a desktop restriction at release.

Inputs: a brushed region over the photo
Inference_Locus: A Firefly model resolves fill for a brushed region from surrounding photo content, non-destructively; variations can be previewed per removal.
Model_Backend: Firefly Image 1 at launch, per source
Date_Note: Early access May 2024 across mobile, desktop, iPad, web, and Classic; Content Credentials attach at GA per source.

Inputs: selection or canvas extension, surrounding image context, optional text prompt, optional reference photo
Inference_Locus: A diffusion model resolves new content for a selection or expanded canvas from surrounding image context and an optional prompt, returned as variations on generative layers. A reference photo can condition object identity, with compositing matched to scale, lighting, and perspective per 2026 coverage.
Model_Backend: Firefly image models; Firefly Fill & Expand default from April 2026; partner models selectable
Date_Note: Shipped 2023; partner-model choice in Photoshop beta September 25, 2025; April 2026 release sets Firefly Fill & Expand as default and drops Firefly Image 3 from the picker, per coverage.
Notes: Seed anchor row (3.0/2.0). April 2026 model-picker detail is from secondary coverage (photoshopnews.com), held provisionally.

Inputs: a composited layer plus its background image
Inference_Locus: A model resolves color, lighting, and shadow adjustments so an inserted element matches its background, invoked per layer. Each use consumes generative credits per Adobe's documentation of the feature.
Date_Note: Teased as Project Perfect Blend at MAX 2024; beta summer 2025; generally available with Photoshop 27.0 around MAX October 2025.
Notes: Available on desktop, web, mobile per coverage.

Inputs: source image plus per-filter sliders (smoothing strength, colorize hints, style choice)
Inference_Locus: Per-filter neural models resolve effects such as skin smoothing, colorization, and style transfer from the source image and slider settings, invoked from the Neural Filters panel. Filters are tiered as featured or beta; some run on-device, others in the cloud.
Date_Note: Introduced with the October 2020 Photoshop release per coverage; featured/beta tiers current.

Inputs: brushed region over the source image; auto-detected distractions (wires, cables, background people)
Inference_Locus: Resolves fill for a brushed or auto-detected region from surrounding image content; Distraction Removal can detect wires, cables, and background people for removal. An options-bar control sets generative AI to auto, on, or off, so fills can run patch-based or generative.
Model_Backend: Firefly-backed when generative option is on
Date_Note: Distraction Removal beta July 2024; in the October 2024 release (Photoshop 26.0).
Notes: One tool spanning patch-based and generative resolution via a toggle.

Inputs: the open image; a click or region for object selection
Inference_Locus: A segmentation model resolves a subject or object mask from the image, invoked from Select > Subject or the Object Selection tool. Output is a selection the designer can refine with manual selection tools.
Date_Note: Shipped in Photoshop 19.1, January 2018.
Notes: Inference produces a boundary; downstream edits remain conventional.

Inputs: source photo, chosen or imported sky asset, edge and tone sliders
Inference_Locus: A model resolves the sky-foreground boundary and masks in the replacement sky; foreground color is retoned toward the chosen sky. Invoked from Edit > Sky Replacement with preset or imported skies.
Date_Note: October 2020 release, Photoshop 22.0.
Notes: Sky content is designer-supplied; inference covers masking and blending.

Inputs: source footage, target aspect ratio, motion preset
Inference_Locus: A model tracks salient action and resolves motion keyframes that keep it framed when a sequence is reformatted to a new aspect ratio. Generated keyframes are editable afterward.
Date_Note: Announced at IBC September 2019; shipped in the late-2019 release.
Notes: Inference emits explicit keyframes, which return to designer control.

Inputs: a recorded dialogue clip tagged in the Essential Sound panel; mix amount
Inference_Locus: A model resolves cleaned dialogue from the recorded clip, attenuating background noise and poor room sound; a mix control blends processed and original audio. Applied per clip.
Date_Note: Shown in beta September 2023 per source; GA timing to be confirmed.

Inputs: an existing clip (video and audio); trim-handle drag sets extension length
Inference_Locus: The Firefly Video Model resolves new frames continuing an existing clip, invoked by dragging past the clip end; audio can extend alongside. Generated media is conditioned on the source clip.
Date_Note: Beta October 2024; generally available April 2, 2025 with 4K and vertical support.
Notes: GA announcement: news.adobe.com/news/2025/04/new-ai-innovation-in-industry.

Inputs: source footage audio; transcript text selections
Inference_Locus: A speech model resolves a transcript from footage; the designer cuts by selecting transcript text and the timeline mirrors those selections. Transcription runs per clip; the resulting edits are conventional cuts.
Date_Note: Generally available May 2023 release.
Notes: Inference supplies an index into the media; resolution of the cut stays explicit.

Inputs: a photograph or single scan of a real-world surface
Inference_Locus: A model resolves a tileable PBR material, with albedo, normal, and roughness maps, from a photograph of a surface; the result becomes a parametric asset for further adjustment in Sampler workflows.
Date_Note: Documented by Adobe Research; shipped in Sampler and Capture.
Notes: Comparable position to photogrammetry: inferred detail sits inside what the photo governs.

Inputs: conversational prompts over a design document; templates and brand assets
Inference_Locus: An assistant resolves design edits and layouts in Express from conversational prompts, executing multi-step changes in the document. Announced at MAX, October 2025.
Date_Note: Announced at MAX October 2025 alongside Firefly Foundry.

Inputs: conversational direction; assets in session
Inference_Locus: An agent resolves multi-step creative tasks from conversational direction, orchestrating image and video generation and tools drawn from Creative Cloud apps; the designer supplies direction and judgment while execution is delegated.
Model_Backend: agentic layer over Firefly and partner models (30+ models per Adobe)
Date_Note: Public beta April 27, 2026.
Notes: June 18, 2026 announcement extends the creative agent across Photoshop, Premiere, Illustrator (news.adobe.com/news/2026/06/adobe-unveils-major-expansion).

Inputs: prompts, dropped reference images, remixing of prior generations on a shared canvas; model choice including partner models
Inference_Locus: A canvas where image and video generations accumulate; new generations can be conditioned on prior ones and on dropped references, with Firefly and partner models selectable. Positioned for pre-production ideation.
Model_Backend: Firefly plus partner models (OpenAI, Google, Runway, Luma, Pika, Ideogram, Moonvalley per coverage)
Date_Note: Shown as Project Concept at MAX London April 2025; generally available late September 2025.
Notes: Canvas persistence and cross-generation conditioning drive the y placement.

Inputs: text prompt, style settings, optional reference image, model choice
Inference_Locus: A text-to-image diffusion model resolves images from prompts and style settings in the Firefly web app, with Firefly and partner models selectable. Image Model 5 can generate at native 4MP and supports prompt-based layered editing, in public beta.
Model_Backend: Firefly Image Model 4; Image Model 5 (public beta); partner models
Date_Note: Image Model 5 public beta announced October 28, 2025 at MAX.
Notes: MAX 2025 release also covers audio generation and the all-in-one studio framing.

Tool: Firefly Text to Video / Generate Video
Inputs: text prompt; camera position, zoom, and motion-type settings; optional reference image; model choice
Inference_Locus: The Firefly Video Model resolves video clips from text prompts, with camera position and motion type specifiable and image conditioning available. Prompt-based editing of generated video and added partner models followed in December 2025 per coverage.
Date_Note: Public beta February 12, 2025; prompt-based video editing and additional partner models December 2025 (TechCrunch).
Notes: Adobe positions generations as commercially safe; stated as vendor claim.

Inputs: text prompt; output type set to subject, scene, icon, or pattern; optional style match to existing artwork
Inference_Locus: The Firefly Vector Model resolves editable vector groups from a text prompt, returning multiple variations; results are placed as paths the designer can rework with standard tools.
Date_Note: Beta with Illustrator 28.0, October 2023; vector generation also runs in the Firefly web app, where partner models are documented.
Notes: Output is addressable vector geometry, which distinguishes it from raster prompt-to-image.

Inputs: plain-language prompts (text or voice) over the open document
Inference_Locus: An agent interprets conversational direction and executes multi-step edits using Photoshop tools on the open document; the designer directs by outcome rather than by operating tools. Working steps are orchestrated by the agent.
Model_Backend: proprietary agentic system over Firefly and Photoshop tooling
Date_Note: Web assistant shown at MAX October 28, 2025; desktop public beta March 10, 2026; wider creative-agent expansion announced June 18, 2026.
Notes: Related: Project Moonlight private beta (March 2026) spans Photoshop, Express, Acrobat per coverage; held provisionally.

Inputs: text prompt; outputs constrained to square, tileable textures
Inference_Locus: A Firefly-powered generator resolves square, tileable texture images from text prompts; outputs can pass into image-to-material conversion for PBR use. Shipped in Sampler 4.4 as beta alongside text-to-pattern and image-to-texture.
Date_Note: Sampler 4.4, beta.
Notes: Prompt-resolved output feeding a conditioned material pipeline.

Inputs: Base geometry, modifier parameters, stack order, sub-object edits
Inference_Locus: Geometry resolves through the modifier stack: non-destructive modifiers applied over base geometry, re-evaluated when parameters change. Polygon, NURBS, and patch toolsets address the model directly.

Inputs: Scene description: geometry, lights, materials, camera, sampling settings
Inference_Locus: Images resolve through unbiased Monte Carlo path tracing from the scene description: lights, materials, and geometry supplied by the designer govern the result; sampling settings trade noise against render time.
Notes: Bundled with Maya and 3ds Max through plugins; CPU and GPU.

Inputs: Commands, coordinates, object snaps, blocks, layers, dimensions
Inference_Locus: Drawing content resolves from direct command input: lines, polylines, blocks, and dimensions placed and edited as addressable objects in the DWG database.
Notes: Sits near the SolidWorks CAD anchor.

Inputs: Building volumes, terrain, site data, program parameters
Inference_Locus: Site and massing models resolve from direct manipulation of building volumes, terrain, and site data in a browser environment; edits propagate to linked analyses.
Notes: Browser-based platform; grew out of Spacemaker.

Inputs: Site and massing model, climate data, analysis parameters
Inference_Locus: Physics-based solvers resolve environmental results (sun hours, daylight, detailed wind CFD, noise propagation) from the site model as cloud jobs, invoked per analysis run.
Notes: These detailed runs supply the training data for the rapid ML analyses.

Inputs: Sketches, dimensions, constraints, features on the parametric timeline
Inference_Locus: Models resolve through the parametric timeline: sketches, features, and constraints recompute downstream geometry when edited.

Inputs: Node attributes, connections, keyframes, deformer weights, scene hierarchy
Inference_Locus: Scene state resolves through Maya's dependency graph: interconnected nodes recompute outputs when inputs or attributes change. The designer addresses geometry, deformers, and animation through node attributes and connections.
Notes: Procedural node architecture; sits near the Houdini SOP anchor.

Inputs: Parametric families, type and instance parameters, constraints, levels and grids
Inference_Locus: Building models resolve through parametric families and constraints: elements hold typed parameters, and dependent geometry and documentation update when parameters change.

Inputs: Source mesh, target face count, edge and feature settings, preprocess options
Inference_Locus: The ReForm solver resolves a new quad topology over a supplied mesh through global optimization, steered by target face count and feature settings; invoked per mesh as a batch computation.
Model_Backend: Autodesk ReForm 1.6; QuadriFlow and Instant Mesh selectable
Date_Note: ReForm 1.6 update ships with 3ds Max 2026 per release notes
Notes: Computational optimization; no learned model documented in sources read.

Inputs: Noisy render, albedo and normal AOVs, imager settings
Inference_Locus: Neural denoisers resolve a cleaned image from the noisy render, conditioned on auxiliary AOVs: OptiX runs on GPU during interactive rendering, OIDN as an imager at render completion. New scenes include the OIDN imager by default.
Model_Backend: NVIDIA OptiX denoiser; Intel Open Image Denoise (OIDN)
Date_Note: OIDN integrated with Arnold 7.0 (2021); OIDN imager default for new scenes since Arnold 7.3.1 per user guide
Notes: y reflects continuous inference during interactive rendering with OptiX.

Inputs: Imported PDF, PNG, or JPG markup overlaid on the drawing in the Trace workspace; can include photographed handwritten markup
Inference_Locus: Cloud ML identifies markups (text, leaders, revision clouds) in an imported file overlaid on the drawing, and can insert them as drawing geometry or surface commands named in markup text (MOVE, COPY, DELETE). Invoked per imported markup file.
Date_Note: AutoCAD 2023 per what's-new documentation (2022 release)
Notes: Cloud processing; internet connection required per docs. Absent from AutoCAD LT and Mac versions per docs.

Inputs: Current drawing content, prior block insertions in the DWG, selected geometry for search-and-convert
Inference_Locus: Machine-learned suggestions resolve from drawing context: placement proposes position and scale based on prior insertions of the same block; replacement suggests substitute blocks; search-and-convert finds repeated geometry and can convert it to block instances. The designer confirms each suggestion.
Date_Note: Placement and Replacement in AutoCAD 2024; Search and Convert added in AutoCAD 2025 (March 2024) per Engineering.com
Notes: Suggestions are advisory; the placed result is an ordinary block instance. Local vs cloud execution undocumented in sources read.

Inputs: Source footage containing human faces
Inference_Locus: ML models recognize facial features in footage and resolve face mattes and a face normal map, invoked per shot; outputs support relighting, color adjustment, and beauty work in the compositing graph.
Date_Note: Face normal map generator in Flame 2020 (2019); ML face segmentation covered April 2020

Inputs: Clip, user-supplied ONNX model, channel mapping in a JSON sidecar file
Inference_Locus: A batch node runs a user-supplied ONNX model over the clip, with input and output channels defined in a JSON sidecar; inference re-runs when the graph renders. 2025.2 added inference on designated RGBA channels.
Date_Note: Flame 2025.1, July 2024; RGBA channel selection in 2025.2
Notes: Opens the ML band to user-chosen models inside an explicit batch graph; governance varies with the loaded model.

Inputs: Source footage; model choice (indoor, outdoor, or external ONNX depth model)
Inference_Locus: ML models resolve a Z-depth map from monocular footage, invoked per shot for depth-based grading and effects. Flame 2027 added indoor and outdoor depth models and can load external ONNX depth models.
Model_Backend: proprietary ML Depth Indoor and Outdoor models; external ONNX depth models loadable
Date_Note: Z-depth generator in Flame 2020 (2019); reworked depth models and ONNX loading in Flame 2027, April 2026, per Digital Production
Notes: Recent change: the April 2026 release opened depth extraction to user-chosen external models.

Inputs: Neighboring frames of the clip, retime settings
Inference_Locus: A learned interpolation model resolves intermediate frames from neighboring frames for slow-motion retimes, invoked per timewarp render.
Date_Note: Flame 2025.1, July 2024, per CG Channel
Notes: Can run in 16-bit or 32-bit depth, CPU or GPU, per coverage.

Inputs: Source footage
Inference_Locus: An ML segmentation model resolves a sky matte from source footage through the semantic keyer, invoked per shot; the matte feeds grading or sky replacement in the compositing graph.
Date_Note: Flame 2020.1, July 2019, per CG Channel
Notes: ML output lands inside an otherwise explicit batch graph.

Inputs: Current massing and site model; wind rose climate data for wind, road and noise sources for noise
Inference_Locus: Neural surrogates trained on detailed-analysis results resolve predicted wind comfort and ground noise from the current massing within seconds, re-predicting as the design changes.
Model_Backend: proprietary surrogates trained on detailed CFD and noise simulation results
Date_Note: Rapid wind June 2023; rapid noise July 2023, per Forma blog
Notes: Wind and noise merged to one row — same mechanism per an Autodesk forum staff reply; can split if the author prefers. Noise source: https://blogs.autodesk.com/forma/2023/07/03/game-changing-rapid-noise-analysis-comes-to-forma-2/

Inputs: Selected faces to connect, bodies to avoid
Inference_Locus: Shape-synthesis algorithms derived from generative design resolve connecting geometry between selected faces, returning several smooth and sharp connection alternatives per run; invoked from the design workspace without load or constraint setup.
Date_Note: Released from technical preview per Engineering.com coverage, Fusion 360 update cycle circa 2022
Notes: Available across license types per coverage.

Inputs: 3D model or assembly, drawing template and style choices
Inference_Locus: The system resolves 2D sheets from a 3D model or assembly: view selection, dimensions, annotations, BOM tables, and fastener exclusion are generated per component against a chosen template. Invoked as a batch generation over the design.
Model_Backend: proprietary (Autodesk AI); mix of learned and rule-based steps per vendor blog
Date_Note: Released May 2025 per Fusion blog
Notes: Can recognize sheet-metal parts and add bend tables; output is editable drawing geometry.

Inputs: Preserve and obstacle geometry, loads, materials, manufacturing methods, design objectives
Inference_Locus: Cloud solvers resolve load-bearing geometry from preserve and obstacle regions, loads, materials, and manufacturing constraints; each study returns multiple outcomes for exploration. Invoked per study as a cloud job.
Date_Note: Help documentation read August 2026; initial ship date predates sources read
Notes: Cloud solve consumes tokens or a simulation extension per docs.

Inputs: Sketch geometry as drawn
Inference_Locus: A Transformer-based model infers likely dimensions and geometric constraints from sketch geometry and proposes them for application; the designer accepts or rejects the suggestions.
Model_Backend: Transformer model trained on constrained-sketch data with classifier-free guidance, per Autodesk Research
Date_Note: Announced Autodesk University October 2024; live by January 2025 per Engineering.com
Notes: Suggestions land as ordinary parametric constraints; the resulting model stays fully explicit.

Inputs: Training animation of the designer's own rig (mocap, keyframes, or Pose Generator randomization) plus driver-control values per frame
Inference_Locus: A trained model approximates a rig's complex deformation from driver-control values, resolving an approximate shape per frame during posing and playback. Training data comes from the rig itself: keyframed or mocap sequences, or randomized poses from the built-in Pose Generator.
Model_Backend: proprietary per-character model, trained in Maya
Date_Note: Maya 2025.2, July 2024, per CG Channel
Notes: Approximation for interactivity; the source rig can be restored at render time. Autodesk suggests it for background and crowd characters. y reflects frame-rate inference during playback.

Inputs: Guide path drawn in the viewport, or start and end position keys; character type (biped, quadruped); action rows in the MotionMaker Editor
Inference_Locus: A learned motion model resolves full-body locomotion for biped and quadruped characters from a guide path drawn in the viewport or from start and end keys; generated motion can be edited as keys afterward. Aimed at previs and layout.
Model_Backend: proprietary; trained on three motion-capture sets (male and female actors, wolf) per coverage
Date_Note: Maya 2026.1, June 2025; model and performance updates in Maya 2026.2, August 2025, per CG Channel
Notes: Band held provisionally as Conditioned; sits near the boundary with Inferential — the path governs trajectory, the gait comes from learned structure. To be confirmed.

Inputs: Dynamo graph authored by the designer, goals, constraints, variable ranges
Inference_Locus: An evolutionary solver generates and ranks design options from a Dynamo graph plus designer-set goals, constraints, and variable ranges; each run resolves a population of alternatives for review.
Model_Backend: Dynamo plus evolutionary optimization; no learned model documented
Date_Note: Shipping with Revit subscription; a 2026 Dynamo forum thread reports no roadmap items for it
Notes: The generative logic itself is designer-authored, which pulls x up. Possibly winding down in favor of Forma, to be confirmed.

Inputs: Text prompt, single or multiple 2D images, sketches, voxels, point clouds, or combinations
Inference_Locus: A generative model resolves 3D shapes from text, images, sketches, voxels, or point clouds, generating shape and texture separately; it can produce functional geometry such as watertight, hollow vessels. Trained on roughly 10 million 3D shapes.
Model_Backend: proprietary experimental model trained on ~10M CAD and organic shapes
Date_Note: Announced May 8, 2024; experimental, unreleased as of sources read (August 2026)
Notes: Research preview, no product integration. Autodesk describes it as groundwork for foundation models across its industries.

Inputs: Node graph over render passes and images
Inference_Locus: Output resolves by evaluating the compositing node graph over render passes; re-evaluation follows graph or input changes. The Denoise node can run OpenImageDenoise inside this graph, a neural step addressable as a node.
Date_Note: Manual current for 5.2 LTS (July 2026); 5.2 added string node support in the Compositor.
Notes: Explicit graph that can host a neural node (Denoise); the graph governs where inference sits.

Inputs: Node graph: input geometry, fields, attributes, exposed parameters
Inference_Locus: Geometry resolves by evaluating the node graph over input geometry and fields; the dependency graph re-evaluates on parameter or input change. Specification stays fully addressable.
Date_Note: In core since 2.92 (2021); 5.0 (Nov 2025) added Volume and SDF nodes; 5.2 LTS (July 2026) added an experimental node-based approach to hair and cloth physics.
Notes: Sits at the Houdini SOP anchor (8.8/3.5): procedural dependency graph, live re-evaluation, zero learned structure.

Inputs: Vertex/edge/face edits; modifier stack parameters
Inference_Locus: Geometry resolves from direct edit operations and the procedural modifier stack; each step is addressable and reorderable in the session. Computation runs on invocation of each tool.
Date_Note: Core mode; manual current for Blender 5.2 LTS (July 2026). Blender 5.0 (Nov 2025) added Array and Scatter on Surface modifiers.
Notes: Anchor row for the explicit end of the Blender ecosystem; comparable to Photoshop Layers in governance.

Inputs: Solver settings, collision geometry, force fields, cache/bake ranges
Inference_Locus: Cloth, rigid-body, and Mantaflow fluid solvers integrate simulation state per frame from designer-set parameters and collision geometry; results bake to caches. Invoked per frame or on bake.
Date_Note: Mantaflow fluids in core since 2.82 (2020); manual current for 5.2 LTS (July 2026).
Notes: Emergent detail from computation, not inference; the parameters govern, the solver accumulates state across frames.

Inputs: Brush strokes, dyntopo/remesh settings
Inference_Locus: The surface resolves from accumulated brush strokes over the mesh; dynamic topology and voxel remeshing recompute tessellation from settings. Computation follows each stroke.
Date_Note: Long-standing core mode; manual current for 5.2 LTS (July 2026).

Inputs: Rendered frame, text prompt, image-similarity strength; animatable settings
Inference_Locus: Stable Diffusion img2img resolves a new image from the Blender render plus a prompt, with a strength setting balancing render against prompt; can run per animation frame with animated settings.
Model_Backend: Stable Diffusion via local Automatic1111 or hosted API; SDXL supported
Date_Note: Repository active through Dec 2025, including a fix for Blender 5.0 compatibility.
Notes: The scene render is the control signal; sits near the Img2Img anchor (5.5/3.0), animation batch mode lifts recurrence.

Inputs: Webcam stream or movie file; target Rigify rig
Inference_Locus: MediaPipe pose, hand, and face estimation resolves landmark motion from camera frames in real time; detected motion transfers to Rigify rigs through computational retargeting. Runs continuously during capture.
Date_Note: Author states active maintenance has stopped, with pull requests considered; repository last pushed Dec 2025. Forked by the freemocap project.
Notes: Frame-rate neural estimation conditioned on live footage — high recurrence with source governance, a corner few Blender modes occupy. Maintenance status flagged; freemocap forks continue the lineage.

Inputs: Noisy render; optional albedo and normal passes; denoiser and quality settings
Inference_Locus: A trained denoiser resolves a cleaner image from the noisy render, conditioned on color plus optional albedo and normal passes. Runs per final frame and continuously during viewport rendered mode.
Model_Backend: Intel Open Image Denoise; NVIDIA OptiX AI denoiser
Date_Note: OptiX viewport denoising added in 2.83 (2020); manual current for 5.2 LTS documents a GPU option for OpenImageDenoise and per-pass prefiltering.
Notes: The neural row inside core Blender. Viewport denoising re-runs at interactive rates (y toward 8); final-render denoise is single-pass per frame (y nearer 2). Candidate marks the viewport mode.

Inputs: Footage, manual or automatic track markers, solve settings
Inference_Locus: Camera pose and sparse scene points resolve by feature tracking and bundle-adjustment solve over supplied footage; solve error is inspectable per track. Invoked on track and solve steps.
Date_Note: Long-standing core feature; manual current for 5.2 LTS (July 2026).
Notes: Conditioned but computational: the footage governs the solve; detail resolved by optimization rather than learned structure. Comparable position to photogrammetry.

Inputs: ComfyUI workflow graph assembled as Blender nodes; scene inputs (viewport captures, depth); model choice
Inference_Locus: Diffusion generation resolves through a user-assembled ComfyUI graph run from inside Blender; scene captures and passes can condition generation for textures and render enhancement. Invoked on graph execution.
Model_Backend: Stable Diffusion family via ComfyUI (local or remote server)
Date_Note: Repository active through Nov 2025; companion bridge ComfyUI-CUP.
Notes: Hybrid case: an explicit, addressable node graph specifies how neural generation runs — graph governance wrapped around inference.

Inputs: Scene depth from the active viewpoint, text prompt, target meshes
Inference_Locus: Depth-to-image Stable Diffusion resolves an image conditioned on scene depth from the current viewpoint; the result projects onto the mesh UVs. Invoked per viewpoint.
Date_Note: Projection mode present from early releases; ControlNet pre-processors added in v0.4.0 (Aug 2024).
Notes: Same addon, different resolution path: scene geometry governs layout, prompt supplies appearance. Separate row from prompt mode on that basis.

Inputs: Scene meshes, defined camera viewpoints, text prompt, ControlNet depth, IPAdapter reference
Inference_Locus: Diffusion models resolve view-consistent textures conditioned on depth from defined camera viewpoints; generated images blend by projection across visible meshes. Invoked per generation pass over the scene.
Model_Backend: SDXL, FLUX.1-dev, Qwen Image Edit via ComfyUI backend
Date_Note: Releases through July 2026; requires Blender 4.2+ / 5.1+.
Notes: Multi-view projection texturing; scene geometry governs where texture lands, diffusion resolves surface appearance.

Inputs: Natural-language direction; scene state returned to the model between steps; optional asset and generation integrations
Inference_Locus: An LLM resolves modeling and scene edits by generating Python that executes in Blender over a socket server, reading scene state back between steps; sessions run multi-step through an MCP client such as Claude Desktop or Cursor.
Model_Backend: Client LLM (Claude and others); optional Hyper3D Rodin and Hunyuan3D generation, Poly Haven and Sketchfab assets
Date_Note: Active through Aug 2026; 25.8k GitHub stars; MIT license.
Notes: Near the LLM Spatial Agent anchor (1.5/6.0); scene inspection between steps pushes recurrence above it. Production runs as generated code, not inspectable working state.

Inputs: Natural-language command in a chat panel; OpenAI API key
Inference_Locus: GPT models resolve Blender Python scripts from English commands and execute them in the open scene. Invoked per command.
Date_Note: Repository dormant since mid-2024; superseded in practice by MCP-style integrations.
Notes: 5k stars. Command-at-a-time scripting without scene read-back; lower recurrence than the MCP agent row.

Inputs: Text prompt, seed/steps, seamless-tiling option
Inference_Locus: Stable Diffusion resolves texture and concept images from a text prompt inside Blender's Image Editor; a seamless option can make results tile. Invoked per generation.
Date_Note: v0.4.1 (Aug 2024) is the newest release, with Blender 4 support from v0.4.0; repository dormant since Aug 2024.
Notes: 8.2k stars. Real and installable; maintenance paused — held provisionally as a historical-current row.

Inputs: Text prompt or reference image in the Meshy webapp; one-click transfer
Inference_Locus: Meshy's hosted models resolve textured meshes from prompts or images in the webapp; the plugin moves results into Blender over a local HTTP bridge and adds print-preparation tools. Generation runs per request on the service.
Date_Note: Plugin v0.6.0; requires Blender 4.2.6+; current as of Aug 2026.
Notes: Generation stays on the hosted service; the Blender side is transfer plus computational cleanup. Image-to-3D runs sit further right than text runs.

Inputs: Text prompts and/or selected media strips (image, video, audio) in the sequencer
Inference_Locus: Local generative models resolve video, image, speech, music, and sound-effect strips from prompts or from selected strips; ControlNet and IP-Adapter options can condition image generation. Invoked per strip generation inside the VSE timeline.
Model_Backend: Hugging Face Diffusers model set, run locally
Date_Note: Active through July 2026; current version targets Blender 5.2+.
Notes: Prompt-to-media inside an editing timeline; strip-to-strip modes (video-to-video, image-to-video) are source-conditioned and sit further right. The timeline holds persistent working context around repeated generations.

Inputs: Single reference image or text prompt; resolution mode
Inference_Locus: TRELLIS.2 resolves a textured 3D mesh from a single image or a text prompt; the mesh imports into the scene for editing or re-texturing. Invoked per generation.
Date_Note: TRELLIS.2 generation documented in the current README; releases through July 2026.
Notes: Same addon, separate resolution path from its texturing mode. Image-conditioned runs sit further right than prompt runs; candidate marks the prompt case.

Inputs: Text prompt, single image, or multiview images; API key
Inference_Locus: Tripo's hosted models resolve textured meshes from text, single-image, or multiview input; results generate through the API and import into the scene. Invoked per generation.
Model_Backend: Tripo hosted models (API); Tripo 2.5 algorithm per vendor blog
Date_Note: Official VAST-AI extension, MIT license; repository active through Nov 2025.
Notes: Multiview mode is source-conditioned and would sit further right (x near 4); candidate marks the text case.

Inputs: Parametric objects, cloner setups, effectors, simulation parameters, node capsules
Inference_Locus: Parametric objects, MoGraph cloners, and the unified simulation framework resolve deterministically from designer-set parameters; 2026.2 adds node-based cloner distribution. Recomputes on change.
Date_Note: Cinema 4D 2026.0 September 10, 2025; 2026.2 April 15, 2026
Notes: 2026.2 also lists a local AI Asset Search for content indexing; the recap identifies no generative features in the desktop 2026 releases.

Inputs: Explicit COP node graph over 2D images and volumes; parameters, solvers, bake targets
Inference_Locus: GPU image-processing context that evaluates an explicit node graph over 2D and volumetric data, recomputing on parameter change. H21 adds a Flow solver (2D fluid via image processing), sparse GPU COP Pyro, and texture baking.
Date_Note: Copernicus context shipped with Houdini 20.5 (2024); described as production-ready for most uses in H21 (August 27, 2025)
Notes: H21 also updates the OIDN render denoiser to 2.2.1 with an ML Train OIDN node for custom denoising filters, per the same source.

Inputs: Node networks, parameters, attributes wired by the designer; every action stored as a node
Inference_Locus: Deterministic evaluation of a designer-authored node network; changes to any node cascade through the graph and recompute the result. No learned structure; resolution is addressable at every node.
Date_Note: Longstanding core; current release Houdini 21, August 27, 2025
Notes: Author anchor row (8.8/3.5). SideFX describes networks as recipes whose changes cascade; assets can encapsulate networks as shareable nodes.

Inputs: Node-based recipe for look development and lighting; USD layers; renderer delegate choice
Inference_Locus: Evaluation of a node-based recipe generates scene data for look development and lighting; Hydra viewports preview through any renderer delegate. Deterministic; no learned structure.
Date_Note: Katana 9.0 current per product page (UsdSuperLayer), 2026
Notes: No machine learning features listed on the product page.

Inputs: A chained stack of grading tools with per-tool parameters, applied to host footage
Inference_Locus: A designer-assembled chain of grading tools evaluates per frame inside the host editor; the Parametric Curve tool (2025.0) manipulates footage via an HDR curve. Deterministic.
Date_Note: Red Giant 2026.0 shipped September 10, 2025; 2026.2.0 December 3, 2025
Notes: Release notes for Red Giant 2025 through 2026.2 show no machine learning features; the suite remains in the computational span of the field as of August 2026.

Inputs: Brush strokes, projection setups, layer stacks or node graph, UDIM texture sets
Inference_Locus: Deterministic evaluation of a layer stack or node graph over UDIM textures; projection painting resolves strokes onto the surface. Smart masks and procedurals are rule-based.
Date_Note: Current product page, 2026; no machine learning features listed
Notes: Multi-channel paint (up to 8 streams from a single node) per product page.

Inputs: Designer-authored node graph, channels, roto, merges, per-node parameters
Inference_Locus: Deterministic per-frame evaluation of a designer-authored node graph. Nuke 16.0 adds Graph Scope Variables, resolving one graph across multiple shots and variations, and ScanlineRender2, a ray-tracing render architecture.
Date_Note: Nuke 16.0 released February 2025

Inputs: Brush strokes with pressure; DynaMesh rebuild triggers; subdivision workflow
Inference_Locus: Brush strokes displace the mesh surface directly; DynaMesh rebuilds topology on demand so sculpting can continue without managing structure. Deterministic response to input.
Date_Note: ZBrush 2026 shipped September 11, 2025 (ZModeler creasing options, Noisemaker 2.0, Python scripting)
Notes: No machine learning features found in ZBrush 2026 coverage (80.lv, September 2025).

Inputs: The designer's rigged character; a pose dataset generated from its joint limits; training run by the designer
Inference_Locus: A network trained on sampled poses of a specific rig resolves skin and tissue deformation from joint transforms, replacing linear blend skinning at playback. Inference runs per frame from the trained model.
Model_Backend: PCA plus neural network; Torch training, ONNX Runtime inference
Date_Note: Content-library example for H20; ML Pose Generate SOP in H20.5 (2024); built-in with custom training recipes in H21 (August 27, 2025)
Notes: Frame-rate inference across a session once trained; the model is specific to the character it was trained on. H21 details per CG Channel.

Inputs: A low-resolution pyro simulation; optionally a custom training run on the designer's own setup
Inference_Locus: A trained network resolves high-resolution volumetric detail conditioned on a low-resolution pyro simulation. An ML Train Volume Upres recipe can fit the model to a specific scenario; inference runs across the frames of the sim.
Date_Note: Shipped in Houdini 21, August 27, 2025

Inputs: Two classes of training images supplied by the designer; source images in the graph
Inference_Locus: A network trained on two image classes resolves output in the target style conditioned on source images, aimed at procedural texture generation. Training runs inside Houdini via the ML Train Style Transfer setup.
Model_Backend: Trainable network via ML Train Style Transfer
Date_Note: Shipped in Houdini 21, August 27, 2025

Inputs: Simulation point clouds; choice of pretrained model; optionally the designer's own training data
Inference_Locus: Pretrained networks resolve a mesh surface from simulation point clouds, with model variants for liquid, granular, and balanced material behavior. Custom models can be trained with a downloadable setup and exported to ONNX. Invoked per frame over sim output.
Model_Backend: Pretrained ONNX models (liquid / granular / balanced variants)
Date_Note: Shipped in Houdini 21, August 27, 2025
Notes: Inferred surface detail sits inside what the point cloud governs.

Inputs: A trained ONNX model file plus input geometry/attributes wired inside a SOP network
Inference_Locus: Runs a supplied ONNX model as a geometry node, mapping input attributes through the trained network on each cook; the node picks an execution provider and can use GPU acceleration. Invoked wherever it sits in the explicit graph.
Date_Note: Documented in the Houdini 20 what's-new machine learning pages (H20, 2023); example-based ML SOP toolset in H20.5 (2024)
Notes: Neural inference embedded in an otherwise explicit SOP graph; H20.5 adds eleven SOP nodes for dataset generation, pre-processing, and inferencing without custom scripts.

Inputs: Input footage; node parameters
Inference_Locus: Pretrained networks built on the CopyCat methodology resolve a 2x resize (Upscale) or motion-blur removal (Deblur) conditioned on input footage, invoked as ordinary nodes in the graph and applied per frame.
Date_Note: Shipped with the Nuke 13 machine learning toolset, 2021

Inputs: Input footage; choice of downloaded model; per-model parameters
Inference_Locus: Third-party pretrained models (depth estimation, segmentation, matting, optical flow, upscaling, style transfer) run in the Inference node, resolving per-frame outputs conditioned on input footage. Models are converted from PyTorch via CatFileCreator.
Model_Backend: Third-party PyTorch models converted to .cat (e.g., Depth Anything, ViTMatte)
Date_Note: Cattery library launched December 2022; models added since
Notes: Foundry-hosted community library; models run locally inside the node graph.

Inputs: Artist-supplied before/after frame pairs from the sequence; training run by the artist; checkpoint loaded into Inference
Inference_Locus: CopyCat trains a network on a small number of artist-made example frames (garbage mattes, beauty repairs, deblur), then the Inference node resolves the learned transformation across the full sequence. Detail beyond the examples is inferred within what they govern.
Date_Note: Shipped in Nuke 13.0, 2021
Notes: Trained checkpoints persist and can be reused across shots; train-review-retrain loop is part of the mode.

Inputs: Source sequence; paint or patch work done on a reference frame
Inference_Locus: SmartVector computes motion vectors from the supplied sequence; VectorDistort takes paint from a reference frame and propagates it through the rest of the sequence along those vectors. Invoked after the artist paints the reference frame.
Date_Note: Longstanding NukeX toolset; current docs
Notes: Vector computation is algorithmic; the propagated result stays inside what the reference paint and footage govern.

Inputs: The rendered lower-resolution frame inside the Octane imager stage; mode choice
Inference_Locus: A learned up-sampler resolves an upscaled frame conditioned on the rendered lower-resolution image, in the Octane imager stage, with progressive and one-stop modes.
Date_Note: Documented in current Octane manuals; introduced after Octane 4

Inputs: In-progress render passes; internal spectral, material, and scene buffers; kernel choice
Inference_Locus: A learned denoiser resolves a cleaned frame conditioned on internal perceptual models of material, spectral irradiance, and scene data before conversion to RGB, running on in-progress frames during path tracing in the viewport.
Date_Note: Shipped with OctaneRender 4 (2018)
Notes: Octane 4 also added AI Light, a learned sampling aid whose performance can improve as more samples render (CG Channel, 2018).

Inputs: The noisy beauty pass plus feature render elements (diffuse, reflection filter) generated by the renderer; engine choice
Inference_Locus: A denoising engine resolves a cleaned frame conditioned on the noisy render and its feature buffers, invoked at end of render or during interactive rendering. Engine options include NVIDIA's AI denoiser and Intel Open Image Denoise alongside a non-learned default; the docs note the NVIDIA engine runs faster and denoises render elements less consistently than the default.
Model_Backend: NVIDIA AI denoiser (OptiX); Intel Open Image Denoise
Date_Note: NVIDIA AI denoiser integration dates to the V-Ray Next generation (2018) per Chaos coverage; current docs list three engines
Notes: The default V-Ray denoiser is non-learned and recommended in docs for render-element consistency; the learned engines trade that for speed.

Inputs: Source mesh; optional guide curves; target polygon count and density settings
Inference_Locus: Resolves new quad topology from a supplied mesh, steered by guide curves and a target polygon count; edge placement inside those constraints is decided by the algorithm. Invoked once per remesh.
Date_Note: Longstanding ZBrush tool; the same retopology shipped in Cinema 4D S26, April 20, 2022
Notes: Algorithmic rather than learned; sits in the Conditioned band because the result is resolved from supplied material rather than addressable specification. ZBrush documentation pages redirected during checks; the Maxon S26 article confirms the tool.

Inputs: Text prompt or reference image
Inference_Locus: Reported integration of Tencent's Hunyuan 3D engine resolving mesh output from a text prompt or reference image, announced first for the iPad edition. Production is resolved through learned structure rather than working state.
Date_Note: Reported mid-2026 announcement; iPad edition public beta at NAB April 2026, commercial release planned late 2026; the desktop 2026 feature recap lists no generative tools
Notes: Source found via search; the page blocked direct fetch, and the C4D 2026 recap I could open makes no mention. Held provisionally as announced, to be confirmed.

Inputs: patch topology, object arguments, messages, UI controls
Inference_Locus: Output follows from the patch: objects connected by patchcords, audio resolved by the MSP signal graph and video by Jitter, live while editing.
Date_Note: Max 9 current per Cycling '74 (2026).

Inputs: node graph, keyframes, exposed parameters
Inference_Locus: Output follows from the node graph — generators, particles, simulations, post chains — evaluated in real time; parameters and connections stay addressable throughout.
Date_Note: Manual current at 2026.1 / 2026.2 (2026).
Notes: Blocks export to media servers; the graph remains the working state end to end.

Inputs: USD layers, references, variants, schemas
Inference_Locus: Scenes resolve from OpenUSD composition — layers, references, variants — authored and rendered through Kit-based applications; the composition stays addressable as structured scene description.
Date_Note: Platform repositioned toward accelerated libraries and microservices for physical-AI simulation per docs.nvidia.com (2025-2026); Kit SDK remains the application framework.
Notes: Generative extensions referenced in NVIDIA blueprint architectures; nothing specific enough sourced this pass for a separate generative-extension row.

Inputs: clips, layer stack, blend modes, effect parameters, live triggering
Inference_Locus: Composited output follows from triggered clips, the layer stack, blend modes, and effect parameters, resolved live by the engine.
Date_Note: Arena/Avenue current per resolume.com (Aug 2026).
Notes: Arena adds projection mapping, edge blending, lighting-desk and SMPTE control on top of Avenue's clip/layer instrument.

Inputs: node patch, parameters
Inference_Locus: Patch output follows from the wired node graph the designer builds; patches load into Arena and Avenue as effects, mixers, and generators.
Date_Note: Wire current per resolume.com (Aug 2026).
Notes: Node-based authoring mode in the same suite; separate row from Arena layer compositing because the working state differs.

Inputs: operator networks, wiring, parameters, Python expressions
Inference_Locus: The operator network cooks continuously; each output follows from wired inputs and designer-set parameters, addressable at any node.
Date_Note: Network Editor documentation current (2026).
Notes: Real-time procedural cooking at frame rate distinguishes it from offline procedural hosts; y placed above Houdini SOP anchor for that reason, held provisionally.

Inputs: scene hierarchy, GameObjects, components, serialized properties, assets
Inference_Locus: Scenes resolve from GameObjects, components, and asset references the designer places and configures; play mode executes the assembled specification.
Date_Note: Manual current for Unity 6.2 (2026).

Inputs: Blueprint graphs, level composition, property values
Inference_Locus: Gameplay and scene behavior follow from node-based Blueprint graphs, level composition, and property values; execution stays traceable through the graph.
Date_Note: Documentation current for UE 5.x (2026).

Inputs: VL patch, node parameters, optional C#/F#
Inference_Locus: Output follows from the VL patch — nodes compiled live in the background, state hot-reloaded — with the running program addressable while it runs.
Date_Note: Stable 7.4 per vvvv.org (Aug 2026).
Notes: Community ML packs exist around vvvv; nothing sourced this pass, so no inference row recorded for it.

Inputs: live audio or latent control input; chosen pretrained model (.ts)
Inference_Locus: The nn~ external runs a pretrained TorchScript model (RAVE, vschaos2, or custom) at audio rate inside the patch: incoming audio or latent control signals decode to audio through the model's learned representation, continuously.
Model_Backend: libtorch / TorchScript; RAVE, vschaos2, user-scripted PyTorch models
Date_Note: v1.6.0 recent per GitHub; adds nn.info model inspection and model download via IRCAM Forum API.
Notes: Timbre and texture resolve from the model's latent space; the input governs temporal structure. Continuous audio-rate inference places y at the top of the range, held provisionally. mc.nn~ / mcs.nn~ multichannel variants for Max 8+.

Inputs: video input; chosen ONNX model; node parameters
Inference_Locus: The AI Model node runs third-party or custom-trained ONNX image models on video inside the node graph — background removal, segmentation, depth and motion estimation, upscaling — and YOLO, AI Face Tracker, and AI Hand Tracker nodes ship as built integrations. Inference recurs per frame on the incoming image.
Model_Backend: ONNX models in Notch; documented examples: Depth Anything (depth), BiRefNet (segmentation), YOLO
Date_Note: Shipped in Notch 2026.2, live as of Aug 2026 per notch.one campaign page; an AI Upscale node is documented back in the 0.9.23 manual.
Notes: 2026.2 also added Manual MCP — the user manual exposed to LLM clients; documentation access rather than a resolution mode, so recorded here as a note. Campaign framing stresses opt-in use.

Software: Omniverse / ACE; plugins for Unreal Engine 5 and Maya
Inputs: voice audio track; character rig mapping
Inference_Locus: The model resolves facial animation — lip sync and expression — from a voice track's acoustic features (phonemes, intonation), streamed in real time or processed per clip; output maps to character facial poses.
Model_Backend: Audio2Face-3D models (open-sourced, with SDK and training framework)
Date_Note: Open-sourced Sept 24, 2025: models, SDKs, training framework, UE5 and Maya plugins.
Notes: Audio governs timing and phoneme structure; expression detail resolves from learned structure. Training framework release means teams can retrain on their own rigs and languages. Coverage: AWN, Sept 2025.

Software: Real-time engines (Unreal, Unity, Omniverse RTX, game runtimes)
Inputs: rendered frames, motion vectors, temporal feedback
Inference_Locus: Transformer models resolve output frames from lower-resolution rendered frames, motion vectors, and temporal feedback; Multi Frame Generation can generate up to five frames per rendered frame. Inference recurs per output frame during rendering.
Model_Backend: DLSS 4 transformer models; DLSS 4.5 second-generation transformer per NVIDIA's DLSS page
Date_Note: DLSS 4 Multi Frame Generation tied to RTX 50-series GPUs (2025); DLSS 4.5 listed on the NVIDIA DLSS page (2026).
Notes: Includes Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, DLAA, Frame Generation. Recorded once as a cross-engine inference row; per-engine integration is plugin (Unreal/Unity) or built into the RTX renderer (Omniverse).

Inputs: live video input, prompt, ControlNet settings; API key for hosted inference
Inference_Locus: Same StreamDiffusionTD control surface; diffusion inference runs on Daydream's hosted GPUs through the Daydream API, returning frames to the TouchDesigner network. Can serve macOS and non-NVIDIA setups.
Model_Backend: StreamDiffusion on Daydream hosted GPUs; SDXL supported
Date_Note: Daydream API live Aug 2025; Scope app and SDXL support announced Nov 2025; an Apr 2026 Daydream post describes hosted mode as the path most macOS TouchDesigner creators use.
Notes: Daydream is Livepeer's real-time AI video effort; product page at daydream.live/streamdiffusiontd; Scope/SDXL announcement via Business Wire (Morningstar, Nov 2025). Same resolution mode as the local row; hosting is the distinction.

Inputs: live video input; model selection
Inference_Locus: The plugin runs Google MediaPipe vision models on live video inside TouchDesigner — face, hand, and pose landmarks, object detection, segmentation, classification — per frame, on device, through an embedded browser runtime.
Date_Note: Distributed as a self-contained .tox for Mac and PC; releases ongoing per GitHub (2025-2026).
Notes: GPU-accelerated, offline-capable; tracking data lands in the network as DAT and TOP outputs for downstream procedural use.

Inputs: live video input; operator parameters
Inference_Locus: Built-in operators run NVIDIA Maxine models on a live video stream: face and body landmark tracking, background matting, denoise. Inference recurs per frame on the incoming image.
Model_Backend: NVIDIA Maxine AR / Broadcast SDK models
Date_Note: Documented in current TouchDesigner docs (2026); AR SDK downloaded separately from NVIDIA.
Notes: Family includes Face Track CHOP, Body Track CHOP, Face Track SOP, Nvidia Background TOP, Nvidia Denoise TOP. Windows and RTX-series GPU required per docs.

Inputs: live video/TOP/NDI input, text prompt, seed and CFG, ControlNets, model choice
Inference_Locus: StreamDiffusion resolves frames from a live input plus prompt, with optional simultaneous ControlNets; low-step diffusion recurs at interactive frame rates inside the network. Can run SD1.5, SD-Turbo, and SDXL locally with TensorRT acceleration.
Model_Backend: StreamDiffusion pipeline; SD1.5 / SD-Turbo / SDXL; TensorRT
Date_Note: v0.3.1 current per dotsimulate docs (2026); StreamV2V added for temporal consistency.
Notes: x moves with denoise strength and ControlNet weight — source-governed at low denoise, prompt-governed at high; 4.2 is a midpoint candidate. Local install: Windows, NVIDIA GPU 6GB+ VRAM, CUDA 12.8.

Inputs: designer-supplied ONNX model; runtime input data
Inference_Locus: The package runs designer-supplied models locally in the editor or in builds, without a network connection; inference recurs wherever the runtime invokes the model, per frame where wired into gameplay.
Model_Backend: Unity Inference Engine (formerly Sentis); ONNX models
Date_Note: Sentis (open beta Nov 2023) renamed Inference Engine at Unity 6.2, Aug 2025; coverage reports the display name back to Sentis at package 2.4.
Notes: Framework row, parallel to Unreal NNE: the mode is embedding model inference into engine execution. Naming in flux across 2025-2026 — record both names.

Inputs: captured facial performance (mono/stereo video, depth, or audio); target MetaHuman rig
Inference_Locus: Facial animation resolves from a captured performance — mono or stereo video, depth data, or audio — solved onto MetaHuman rig controls; processing can run offline per take or in real time from a webcam, mobile capture, or audio stream.
Date_Note: Released June 2023; real-time mono video/webcam and audio-driven paths documented for UE 5.6 (2025).
Notes: The performance governs the result tightly; the solver's learned mapping fills rig-space detail. Real-time capture mode raises recurrence toward the frame-rate band — y candidate reflects the per-take path.

Inputs: designer-generated simulation training data (Maya); skeletal animation at runtime
Inference_Locus: A model trained on designer-generated simulation data (muscle, flesh, cloth) approximates the deformation at runtime, conditioned on skeletal pose each frame. Training and inference stay on the GPU via the engine's Deformer Graph.
Model_Backend: Neural Morph and Nearest Neighbor models via engine neural inference + Deformer Graph
Date_Note: In UE since 5.0-era; docs current at 5.8 (2026).
Notes: The training set is designer-supplied simulation, so the learned structure is itself specified upstream — a case where conditioning includes the training data, distinct from vendor-pretrained rows.

Inputs: pretrained ONNX model; input tensors from engine data
Inference_Locus: NNE provides a common engine API that can load and run pretrained ONNX models on CPU or GPU, at runtime or in the editor; the designer supplies the model and the calling context, and inference recurs wherever invoked.
Model_Backend: ONNX via runtime plugins (NVIDIA TensorRT for RTX, Intel OpenVINO, others)
Date_Note: Overview documented for UE 5.7/5.8 (2025-2026); an earlier Neural Network Inference plugin dates to UE 5.0 per Intel's guide.
Notes: Framework row: the mode is embedding arbitrary model inference into engine execution; targeted uses per docs include animation, mesh deformation, denoising, physics augmentation.

Inputs: natural-language direction; open project context
Inference_Locus: The Assistant resolves editor actions from natural-language direction: it can inspect the open project, answer technical queries, run routine tasks, and write code, iterating across a session with project context.
Date_Note: Unity AI shipped with Unity 6.2, Aug 2025.
Notes: Placement near the LLM Spatial Agent anchor (1.5/6.0), held provisionally.

Inputs: text prompt; reference and style options
Inference_Locus: Generators resolve sprites, textures, materials, animations, and sounds from text prompts through Unity and partner models, invoked per generation inside the editor.
Model_Backend: Scenario and Layer LoRAs (Stable Diffusion / Flux-based) for sprites; Unity text-to-texture and text-to-animation models; Kinetix video-to-animation
Date_Note: Unity AI shipped with Unity 6.2, Aug 2025, replacing Muse; priced in Unity Points.
Notes: Kinetix video-to-animation path is source-conditioned; the row sits at the prompt-driven mode. Coverage (Digital Production, Aug 2025) places copyright responsibility with the user.

Inputs: clips on the timeline; node graph of corrections; keyframed parameters
Inference_Locus: The timeline and node graph carry the specification; output re-renders deterministically from clip edits, node connections, and keyframed parameters. The color page evaluates the node graph on each change.
Date_Note: Resolve 21 current per Blackmagic product page, August 2026; Resolve 21 also adds AI Speech Generator, CineFocus, Face Age Transformer, UltraSharpen, Motion Deblur per the what's-new page.
Notes: Node-based grading; placement near the Houdini SOP anchor, held provisionally.

Inputs: clips; storyline arrangement; connected clips; effect parameters
Inference_Locus: Resolution is computational: the magnetic timeline repositions connected clips deterministically as the designer edits, and effects render from set parameters.
Date_Note: Core model since FCP X (2011); FCP 11 current line, released November 13, 2024.

Inputs: spoken audio in the clip; language and style choices
Inference_Locus: Speech recognition resolves caption text from the clip's audio; styling applies from templates the designer picks. Text-to-speech and voice enhancement run in the same feature family.
Date_Note: Listed on the CapCut tools pages, August 2026.
Notes: CapCut also carries conditioned image/video tools on the same pages: background removal, people removal, inpainting, image enhancement.

Inputs: the production script; spoken audio in the media clips
Inference_Locus: Speech transcription is matched against a supplied script and a timeline resolves from the matches, with alternate takes placed on lower tracks. Invoked once per script; the designer edits the assembled timeline afterward.
Date_Note: Shipped with Resolve 20 (announced April 2025).
Notes: Resolve 20 also added AI Multicam SmartSwitch: angle switching resolved from active-speaker analysis, same source.

Inputs: a highlighted frame region; a text prompt; the surrounding frame
Inference_Locus: A generative model resolves image content for a highlighted region from a text prompt conditioned on the surrounding frame, filling areas left by reframing or limited coverage. Invoked per region.
Date_Note: Shipped with Resolve 20; announced April 2025, described in the sourced article July 2025.
Notes: Placement mirrors the Photoshop Generative Fill anchor: prompt plus mask plus surrounding image.

Inputs: footage; the resulting matte feeds grades or effects the designer places
Inference_Locus: A depth-estimation network resolves a per-pixel depth matte from each frame, conditioned on the footage. The matte can drive grades, blurs, or atmosphere the designer applies on top.
Date_Note: Listed as 3D Depth Map on the Studio page, August 2026.

Inputs: paint strokes or points on a subject; the footage itself
Inference_Locus: A segmentation network resolves a subject matte from rough strokes or points and tracks it across frames, conditioned on the footage. Invoked per subject on the Color page; the designer can refine with further strokes.
Date_Note: Magic Mask 2 shipped with Resolve 20 (2025) with point selection and paint refinement; listed again in Resolve 21 what's-new, August 2026.
Notes: y reflects frame-to-frame track propagation; the mask at one frame conditions the next.

Inputs: footage; a virtual light the designer places and aims
Inference_Locus: Surface geometry inferred from the frame lets a placed virtual light resolve as shading on the scene, conditioned on the footage. Invoked as a Resolve FX on the Color page.
Date_Note: Recalled as shipping in the Resolve 18.x cycle; the Blackmagic pages fetched in August 2026 confirm 3D Depth Map and other Neural Engine FX, with Relight absent from them.
Notes: Feature named in the task brief; kept with unverified status pending a source that names it.

Inputs: source clip; scale factor; sharpness and noise settings
Inference_Locus: An upscaling network resolves added pixel detail from the source frames; inferred detail sits inside what the footage governs. Applied per clip as a render-time process for 4K/8K delivery from lower-resolution sources.
Date_Note: Long-standing Studio feature; 3x and 4x enhanced upscaling shipped with Resolve 20 (2025).
Notes: y raised above still-image upscaling for per-frame inference across the clip, held provisionally.

Inputs: a voice recording; a strength setting

Software: Veras (in Rhino, SketchUp, Revit, Archicad, Vectorworks, Forma)
