Inference_Locus: A multi-step research agent plans, retrieves across tenant and web content, and composes cited reports from a question-level prompt.
Model_Backend: OpenAI deep-research models; Claude Sonnet 4 and Opus 4.1 selectable since Sept 2025; Anthropic models enabled by default for most commercial tenants Jan 7, 2026
Date_Note: Anthropic default enablement Jan 7, 2026 per Directions on Microsoft; regional defaults vary (off in EU/EFTA/UK and government clouds pending admin action).
Notes: First surface where Claude appeared in M365 Copilot (Sept 2025, alongside Copilot Studio).

Inputs: board content as context — frames, timelines, kanbans, diagrams; team material from connected sources
Inference_Locus: Agent sidekicks resolve contributions from accumulated board context, building on existing team material in Miro and connected tools; the vendor frames the canvas itself as the prompt.
Date_Note: Listed on miro.com/ai as of Aug 2026.
Notes: Earlier discrete Miro AI features (diagram from prompt, sticky-note clustering) no longer appear on the AI landing page; current framing centers Sidekicks and Flows.

Inputs: prompt; page content; workspace context; connected-app content via Enterprise Search
Inference_Locus: The system drafts and revises page content from prompts with workspace context available; invoked inline per block or from the AI panel. Research Mode can compose longer reports from gathered sources.
Date_Note: Current product page, accessed Aug 2026.
Notes: Vendor page leaves model backends unstated.

Inputs: agent instructions; workspace pages and databases; connected tools (Slack, Drive, GitHub, calendars); schedules, triggers, shared docs
Inference_Locus: Configured agents run multi-step work on schedules or event triggers, on or off hours, acting across the workspace and connected apps; runs consume usage credits and are audit-logged.
Model_Backend: unspecified; external agents (Claude, Cursor, Codex) attachable via the 3.5/3.6 developer platform
Date_Note: Active through 2026: developer platform (Notion 3.5) May 13, 2026; Notion 3.6 Jul 1, 2026 added external agents and Office file support; AI Meeting Notes can trigger agents since Jul 31, 2026; free agent runs ended May 3, 2026.
Notes: High-recurrence end of the category: standing agents with triggers, credits, and audit logs.

Inputs: chat prompt; clarifying answers; web research the agent performs
Inference_Locus: From a chat prompt outside the target app, the system produces complete Word documents or PowerPoint decks through multi-step research and build.
Model_Backend: Anthropic models, per Microsoft's launch announcement
Date_Note: Introduced Sept 29, 2025 in the Frontier program.
Notes: Anthropic-powered at launch — part of the answer to the Anthropic-in-M365 verification question.

Inputs: text prompt, pasted content, or uploaded file (PDF, DOCX, PPTX)
Inference_Locus: The system generates a zoomable presentation from a prompt or uploaded file, building an outline and applying layout automatically; per-element text refinement and image generation can follow.
Date_Note: Current feature page, accessed Aug 2026.
Notes: Output lands in Prezi's zoomable canvas format rather than linear slides; the canvas itself remains hand-editable.

Inputs: prompt (historical mode)
Inference_Locus: Historically generated narrative presentations from prompts. Current state unconfirmed: tome.app returned 404 on Aug 12, 2026, tome.com failed to resolve, and earlier coverage described a pivot away from presentations.
Date_Note: Site unreachable Aug 12, 2026.
Notes: Kept as a field-status row: named in the category list, apparently defunct or relocated. To be confirmed before any placement.

Inputs: Clips, MIDI notes, warp markers, device chains, automation lanes, routing
Inference_Locus: Resolution is deterministic: audio follows clip playback, device DSP, and automation the designer addresses directly. Machine inference sits outside this mode.
Date_Note: Live 12 is the current major version (released 2024); 12.3 point release adds features listed in separate rows
Notes: Explicit anchor for the DAW family; parallel to the Photoshop Layers seed placement.

Inputs: Tracks, clips, fades, plugin chains, automation, mixer routing
Inference_Locus: Resolution is deterministic: recorded audio and MIDI follow edits, routing, plugin DSP, and automation the designer addresses directly.
Date_Note: Pro Tools 2026.4 current per coverage (2026)
Notes: Second Explicit anchor; recording and mixing workflow rather than clip-launch arrangement.

Inputs: A query sample or Core Library preset; the analyzed library it searches against
Inference_Locus: A neural network computes similarity scores between a query sample and library sounds from spectral and temporal characteristics, timbre, and pitch; the first two seconds of each file are analyzed in the background. Invoked per search from the browser or a Drum Rack; the result is a ranked list the designer picks from.
Date_Note: Shipped with Live 12 (2024)
Notes: Retrieval mode: inference selects existing samples; audio content stays untouched. Preset search covers Core Library and Factory Packs.

Inputs: An audio clip or file; a choice among vocals, drums, bass, other; quality or speed mode
Inference_Locus: Neural source separation resolves vocals, drums, bass, and other parts from a mixed audio file, invoked per clip from the browser, Session, or Arrangement View. Processing runs locally.
Date_Note: Live 12.3 (2025; release month to be confirmed); included in Live Suite from 12.3
Notes: 12.3 also added Splice integration in the browser (per press coverage).

Inputs: The exported track; genre preset and loudness target selection
Inference_Locus: A cloud service resolves a mastered render from the uploaded track under genre-tuned presets and loudness targets for streaming platforms. Invoked per export from inside FL Studio.
Date_Note: FL Cloud with mastering shipped with FL Studio 21.2 (late 2023)

Inputs: A finished song file dropped into the project
Inference_Locus: The Remix tool detects tempo and resolves drums, bass, instruments, and vocals from a mixed song in one operation, inside the DAW, locally.
Date_Note: Stem separation appeared in FL Studio 21.2 (2023); one-click Remix flow in FL Studio 2026 (July 7, 2026)

Inputs: An uploaded mix (WAV/AIFF recommended); mastering style choice; optional reference track; album batches
Inference_Locus: An engine trained on the adjustments mastering engineers make analyzes the uploaded track and resolves EQ, compression, stereo imaging, and loudness for release; style selection and an optional reference steer the outcome.
Date_Note: Product page current August 2026; version dates unpublished by the vendor

Inputs: The stereo mix at the output; character selection and setting adjustments after analysis
Inference_Locus: Analyzes the project's mix and applies EQ, dynamics, and loudness processing toward release targets; the designer can adjust character and settings after the analysis pass.
Date_Note: Listed in the current App Store feature set (Aug 2026); shipped with the October 2023 Logic Pro 10.8 update, date to be confirmed against Apple release notes

Inputs: Chord track, style choice, complexity and intensity parameters, kit or patch selection
Inference_Locus: Generated bass, keyboard, and drum performances resolve from the session's chord progression and per-player parameters, and regenerate as the designer edits chords or settings. Apple describes the players as AI-driven, extending the earlier Drummer.
Date_Note: Bass Player and Keyboard Player added May 2024, joining Drummer
Notes: Performance content is parameter-governed; band held provisionally between Explicit and Conditioned.

Inputs: A stereo audio recording
Inference_Locus: On-device neural separation resolves four parts — vocals, drums, bass, other instruments — from a mixed stereo file, invoked per region. Runs on Apple silicon.
Date_Note: Logic Pro for Mac 11 and Logic Pro for iPad 2, May 13, 2024

Inputs: An uploaded song
Inference_Locus: Resolves isolated vocals, instruments, and drums from an uploaded song, alongside chord detection, transcription, and speed and pitch adjustment. AI Studio can generate instrumental stems from the track's context; Voice Studio can resolve vocal parts from models trained on singers.
Date_Note: Product site current August 2026; iPad App of the Year 2024, Apple Design Awards finalist 2025
Notes: AI Studio and Voice Studio are generative modes conditioned on the user's track; a split into separate rows is possible if the author wants finer grain.

Inputs: A supplied melody line; for JASCO, chords, melody, and drum tracks; text style direction
Inference_Locus: Melody conditioning steers generation to follow a supplied melodic line; JASCO resolves music conditioned on chords, melody, and drums together with text. MusicGen Style adds text-and-style-to-music conditioning.
Date_Note: Per repository, current August 2026; JASCO a later addition, date unstated on the fetched page

Inputs: A designer-chosen loop region of track or bus audio; Tone, Dynamics, Saturation, Width intent controls
Inference_Locus: Auditions a loop of the material and resolves a custom signal chain with macro controls across the plugins it manages; the designer adjusts intent panels after the pass.
Date_Note: Neutron 5 released October 30, 2024

Inputs: The mix on the master bus; a reference file; module choices, LUFS target, genre modifiers in the custom flow
Inference_Locus: Analyzes program audio and resolves a mastering chain by matching tone, dynamics, and width toward a reference or genre target; the custom flow exposes module selection and loudness targets before the chain is applied.
Date_Note: Ozone 12 released September 2025
Notes: Ozone 12 also adds ML modules working inside a stereo file: Stem EQ (per-stem EQ within a mix), Unlimiter (dynamics restoration), Bass Control.

Inputs: Clip audio handed to the ARA plugin; note-level or parameter edits inside the plugin view
Inference_Locus: ARA plugins read clip audio in place and resolve an editable analysis — pitch and timing material, vocal alignment, synthesized voice — which the designer then edits at note or parameter level. Supported partners include Waves Sync Vx and Dreamtonics Synthesizer V.
Date_Note: ARA plugin support expanded in Pro Tools 2025.12 per coverage
Notes: Analysis is source-governed; the working state after analysis is addressable, which holds x high within the Conditioned band.

Inputs: Recorded dialogue or vocal audio on tracks
Inference_Locus: Speech recognition resolves text transcriptions from track audio for dialogue and lyric workflows. From 2026.4, transcription data carries through AudioSuite renders, commits, consolidations, and session exports.
Date_Note: Shipped in Pro Tools 2025.6 (June 2025); carry-through expanded in 2026.4
Notes: NAB 2026 previews list further speech-to-text work and an fPost (Forte AI) partner integration, unshipped at coverage time — designed, unexecuted per that source.

Inputs: A mixed recording; separation targets and sensitivity controls
Inference_Locus: Neural networks resolve dialogue or vocal apart from surrounding noise and reverb, offline or in realtime plugin form. RX 12 adds Scene Rebalance for independent level control of elements inside a stereo mix and Stems View for editing isolated components.
Date_Note: RX 12, April 2026; realtime plugin versions added in this release
Notes: The realtime plugin versions can run continuously in a session, which pushes recurrence above the offline passes.

Inputs: The audio file or selection; accept-or-adjust decisions on proposed fixes
Inference_Locus: Analyzes the recording, recognizes problems — clicks, clipping, hum, noise, reverb — and proposes a repair chain the designer can adjust before rendering. Invoked per file or selection.
Date_Note: RX 12 released April 29, 2026, with rebuilt neural networks for core modules

Inputs: The playing track; pad and FX gestures selecting which stems sound
Inference_Locus: Realtime source separation resolves vocals, melody, bass, and drums from the playing track during performance, invoked from performance pads, with stem-specific echo and breaker effects for transitions.
Date_Note: Introduced with Serato DJ Pro 3.0 (launch coverage October 2022); later in DJ Lite; pad modes expanded in 3.1
Notes: High recurrence from continuous frame-rate inference during live performance; source governance stays high — an unusual corner of the field.

Inputs: A style choice from twelve starting points; layer swaps and level moves on the resulting stack
Inference_Locus: The system resolves a stack of up to eight catalog samples matched by key, tempo, and compatibility from a chosen style; the designer swaps layers, adjusts levels, and exports stems or an Ableton Live set.
Date_Note: Launched June 7, 2023, on the Splice website; Stack creation earlier in the CoSo app
Notes: Band held provisionally: direction is sparse while the result stays layer-addressable and drawn from existing samples.

Inputs: Input audio; a selected region for inpainting; text direction
Inference_Locus: Audio-to-audio and inpainting resolve new material from supplied audio: the designer places input audio, selects where generation starts, and the model continues or fills the region from its context.
Date_Note: Inpainting introduced with 2.5, September 2025; audio-to-audio carried over from 2.0
Notes: Placement parallels the masked-inpainting seed anchor.

Inputs: Uploaded or recorded audio; a target style; for Voices, the user's own verified singing voice
Inference_Locus: Covers keeps a song's melody and resolves it into a different style from uploaded audio. Voices matches singing in uploaded audio to the user's verified voice; the voice stays private to its creator.
Date_Note: Covers September 12, 2024; Voices with v5.5 March 2026, on iOS and Android August 7, 2026

Inputs: Natural-language prompts; the open Live Set as readable state
Inference_Locus: An LLM client resolves session edits — track and clip creation, MIDI note insertion, device loading, tempo, transport — from prompts, via an MCP server bridged to a Remote Script socket inside Live. Runs as a multi-step loop that can read session state between actions.
Model_Backend: MCP client LLM (Claude Desktop, Cursor); community MCP servers
Date_Note: Community projects with directory coverage and setup guides through 2026; start dates to be confirmed
Notes: Third-party, unofficial. Several parallel implementations (ahujasid; jpoindexter with 200+ tools, REST API, Max for Live). Placement parallels the LLM Spatial Agent seed.

Inputs: Natural-language requests inside the DAW; the open project as context
Inference_Locus: An in-DAW chatbot resolves actions in the open project from natural-language requests and can execute tasks agentically. Image-Line states user data is excluded from training.
Date_Note: FL Studio 2026 (July 2026) per coverage
Notes: Built into the DAW, distinct from the third-party MCP route in Ableton. LLM backend undocumented in sources consulted.

Inputs: Text description; model variant choice
Inference_Locus: A controllable text-to-music model resolves audio from text descriptions. Runs locally from open weights through the AudioCraft library; AudioGen and MAGNeT cover text-to-sound and non-autoregressive generation in the same library.
Date_Note: Initial releases 2023; repository current as of August 2026 — dates unstated on the fetched page
Notes: Open weights; also embedded in third-party tools. Research library rather than end-user product.

Inputs: Text prompt; duration and structure direction
Inference_Locus: The model resolves music and sound up to about three minutes from text prompts, with multi-part structure (intro, development, outro). A three-minute track can generate in under two seconds per Stability; trained on licensed data per the vendor.
Date_Note: Stable Audio 2.5 released September 2025; available via web, API, fal, Replicate, ComfyUI, on-premises

Inputs: Text prompt; optional custom lyrics, style tags, duration slider
Inference_Locus: The model resolves full songs — vocals, arrangement, mix — from text prompts and optional lyrics. v5.5 outputs 48kHz audio with stem export; My Taste applies learned user preference to generations via the Magic Wand.
Date_Note: v5.5 released March 26, 2026; licensed industry-partnered models announced for later 2026
Notes: Custom Models (train a personal v5.5 on 6+ uploaded tracks) shifts conditioning toward the user's own material; held in this row pending author ruling.

Inputs: Uploaded samples and stems; multitrack timeline edits; per-track generation requests
Inference_Locus: A generative audio workstation: the designer uploads material, generates stem variations, and edits in a multitrack timeline, with export to audio or MIDI for DAW use. Generation and arrangement recur across the session.
Date_Note: Released September 25, 2025, for Premier subscribers
Notes: Sits between prompt services and DAWs: inferential resolution with a persistent, addressable timeline.

Inputs: Text prompt, lyrics, style tags; extension and remix controls on prior generations
Inference_Locus: The model resolves songs from prompts and lyrics, with extension and remix passes on prior output. During the transition to the licensed platform, creations stay inside the Udio environment, with fingerprinting and filtering added.
Date_Note: UMG settlement October 29, 2025; licensed platform with UMG (and a Warner agreement) announced for 2026
Notes: Production conditions in flux: the 2026 platform is announced, unshipped per sources — designed, unexecuted.

Inputs: RAW file; layer stack; hand-drawn masks; curve, color, and slider values
Inference_Locus: The engine renders the RAW deterministically from the parameter set — layer stack, hand-drawn masks, curves, color edits. Each settings change re-renders from the same addressable specification.
Date_Note: long-standing core mode; current per vendor feature page, Aug 2026
Notes: Explicit anchor for the category; sits near Photoshop Layers (8.5/2.0) in the seed.

Inputs: RAW file; detected camera and lens pair matching a lab-measured module
Inference_Locus: Distortion, vignetting, chromatic aberration, and lens-softness corrections resolve from lab-measured profiles for the detected camera–lens pair. The correction is deterministic per module.
Date_Note: 100,000+ camera/lens module combinations per April 2025 review
Notes: Profiles are vendor-measured rather than designer-authored; Explicit placement held provisionally.

Inputs: source image; a button press (Subject, Background, People) or a marquee drawn for AI Select
Inference_Locus: A segmentation model resolves a mask from the source image when the designer invokes Subject, Background, or People selection, or draws a marquee for AI Select. The mask becomes an editable layer mask; adjustments applied through it are parametric.
Date_Note: Subject/Background/AI Select in 16.3 per coverage; People masking added in 16.5, late 2024 per coverage
Notes: Inference resolves the selection; the edit itself stays explicit. Hybrid placement held provisionally.

Inputs: source image; a reference photo whose look is to be matched
Inference_Locus: The system estimates develop settings that move the source toward the reference photo's color and tone. Output is a set of editable parameters, resolved once per invocation.
Date_Note: shipped in 16.5, late 2024 per coverage
Notes: Reference-conditioned parameter estimation; the result lands as inspectable slider values.

Inputs: designer-authored node graph; loaded model files; source images or folders
Inference_Locus: The designer authors a node graph chaining model inference with computational image operations; each run resolves the graph over the inputs. Orchestration is addressable; per-node upscaling resolves through the loaded model.
Model_Backend: user-loaded models via PyTorch (Spandrel), NCNN, ONNX, TensorRT
Date_Note: active development per repo, Aug 2026
Notes: Explicit graph wrapping learned resolution — a boundary case between Explicit and Conditioned; band held provisionally.

Inputs: RAW sensor data; engine choice (DeepPRIME 3, XD2s, XD3 X-Trans); optional local masks for selective strength; output format
Inference_Locus: A neural engine jointly denoises, demosaics, and corrects residual chromatic shifts from RAW sensor data in one batch pass before creative editing elsewhere. Output is a Linear DNG that keeps parametric editability downstream.
Model_Backend: DeepPRIME 3 / DeepPRIME XD2s / DeepPRIME XD3 X-Trans
Date_Note: PureRAW 5 released April 15, 2025; DeepPRIME XD3 X-Trans out of beta in PureRAW 5.3 per DxO news; XD3 for Bayer slated for PureRAW 6 in 2026 per coverage
Notes: Inference reconstructs the demosaic; the creative edit happens downstream in other software. PureRAW 6 claim is designed, unshipped.

Inputs: source image; model choice (Standard, High Fidelity, Low Resolution, Text & Shapes, Art & CGI); scale factor; detail/denoise sliders
Inference_Locus: A CNN upscaler resolves added pixel detail from the source image at the chosen scale, model, and slider settings. Core models run locally; added detail stays within what the source governs.
Model_Backend: proprietary CNN models (Standard v2, High Fidelity v2/v3, Low Resolution v2, Text & Shapes, Art & CGI)
Date_Note: current model lineup per docs, Aug 2026
Notes: Source-conditioned upscaling; sits near ControlNet Depth (6.8) on x.

Inputs: very low-resolution source (about 1MP or less); detail slider; optional pre-downscaling
Inference_Locus: A generative model reconstructs plausible detail for sources near 1MP or below, governed by the source image and a detail slider. Cloud rendering is recommended for larger inputs.
Date_Note: Recover introduced in v7.1.0; pre-downscaling added in v8.4.0 per docs
Notes: Generative reconstruction where source detail is largely absent.

Inputs: source image; creativity level (Low to Max); free-text image description; texture slider
Inference_Locus: A diffusion-based model regenerates the image at higher resolution; a creativity setting and a text description shift how far output can depart from the source. At higher creativity the description carries more of the resolution.
Model_Backend: proprietary diffusion (Redefine Realistic / Redefine Creative, labeled beta in docs)
Date_Note: shipped with Gigapixel 8, late 2024; Realistic/Creative split per 8.2 coverage, Feb 2025; beta label in docs as of Aug 2026; subscription-first pricing shift Oct 2025 per coverage
Notes: Near the Conditioned–Inferential boundary at Max creativity; Face Recovery disabled in Creative mode per docs. Photoshop 2026 exposes it inside Generative Upscale per coverage.

Inputs: source image; brush mask over the object to remove
Inference_Locus: A diffusion inpainting model resolves fill for the masked region from surrounding image context; vendor guidance recommends one object per pass. Results collect in a Generative Creations folder.
Date_Note: GenErase released October 26, 2023; GenExpand and GenSwap followed through Nov–Dec 2023

Inputs: expanded crop frame (up to 25% per iteration); optional text prompt
Inference_Locus: Outpainting resolves border content for an extended canvas, up to 25% per iteration, from image context plus an optional prompt.
Date_Note: rolled out Nov–Dec 2023 per Skylum newsroom

Inputs: brush mask locating the region; short noun prompt naming the replacement
Inference_Locus: A generative model resolves a replacement object matching a short text prompt inside a mask-located region. The mask governs placement; the prompt supplies the content.
Date_Note: rolled out Nov–Dec 2023 per Skylum newsroom
Notes: Near the Conditioned–Inferential boundary; prompt carries the content, mask carries the location. Band held provisionally.

Inputs: source photo; chosen sky asset (bundled or custom); relight and blend sliders
Inference_Locus: A segmentation model resolves the sky region; the chosen sky composites in with automatic relighting of the foreground. Sliders adjust the blend parametrically.
Date_Note: long-standing feature, current per vendor page Aug 2026; a Fall 2026 upgrade (Enhance AI 2.0, AI Assistant 2.0) is slated per vendor page — designed, unshipped
Notes: The replacement sky is designer-chosen material; inference locates and blends it.

Inputs: source image; brushed region over the distraction
Inference_Locus: Generative fill resolves replacement content for a brushed region from surrounding image context, invoked per erase.
Date_Note: listed among Photo RAW 2026 AI tools per vendor announcement, late 2025

Inputs: RAW or rendered image; noise and detail sliders
Inference_Locus: A noise-reduction network resolves a cleaned image from the source, with sliders scaling its effect. Runs inside Photo RAW and as a plugin for other hosts.
Date_Note: current in Photo RAW 2026, announced late 2025 per vendor press; 2026.5 update current Aug 2026

Inputs: source image; model choice (generative Highest Quality model or faster standard model); target size
Inference_Locus: A generative super-resolution model recreates fine detail, restores sharpness, and removes artifacts at the target size; a faster standard model is the alternative choice. Built into the Photo RAW 2026 core application.
Model_Backend: Resize AI 2026 (proprietary; generative Highest Quality model)
Date_Note: Resize AI 2026 folded into core Photo RAW 2026, announced late 2025 per vendor
Notes: Formerly a separate Resize app; generative model targets extreme crops and low-quality sources per vendor copy.

Inputs: source image; a click on the object to select
Inference_Locus: A segmentation model resolves an object mask from a single click; the mask then carries parametric adjustments or filters as a layer.
Date_Note: current in Photo RAW 2026 per vendor pages, Aug 2026
Notes: Same pattern as Capture One AI Masking: inferred selection, explicit edit.

Inputs: source image; per-step overrides of detected models and settings
Inference_Locus: The system inspects each image, selects enhancement models and settings (denoise, sharpen, upscale, face recovery), and applies them as a stack the designer can override step by step before export.
Date_Note: Autopilot present since Photo AI 1.0 (2022); 'intelligent autopilot' revision in Photo AI 4, May 2025 per vendor announcement
Notes: System-selected pipeline over a supplied source; recurrence comes from stacked models per session.

Inputs: source image; brushed selection over the object or damage
Inference_Locus: Generative fill resolves replacement content for brushed regions — object removal in a dedicated workspace, plus a dust-and-scratch mode for film scans. Content is inferred from surrounding image context.
Date_Note: Remove workspace and Dust & Scratch removal in Photo AI 4, May 2025 per vendor announcement
Notes: Mask-conditioned inpainting; sits between Inpainting masked (4.5) and Generative Fill (3.0) anchors.

Inputs: source image; brush-selected region; strength slider; local or cloud render choice
Inference_Locus: A generative deblur model reconstructs detail in out-of-focus or blurred regions the designer selects by brush. Rendering can run locally or through cloud processing.
Date_Note: Super Focus shipped 2024; v2 out of beta with Photo AI 4, May 2025; v3 current per docs, Aug 2026
Notes: Detail is generated where the source is blurred; brush region bounds the effect.

Inputs: source photo; the detected scene workflow can be reassigned; sliders refine the result
Inference_Locus: A classifier detects the scene type (portrait, landscape, birds, pets) on load and applies scene-specific corrections to color, lighting, and noise automatically. The designer can reassign the workflow and adjust the result parametrically.
Date_Note: Radiant Photo 2 current per vendor site; reviews 2024–2025
Notes: Inference picks the correction recipe; corrections themselves land as adjustable parameters.

Inputs: image file; model choice; output scale and tile size; optional GFPGAN face-enhance flag
Inference_Locus: A GAN-based restoration model trained on synthetic degradations resolves upscaled, artifact-cleaned output per invocation via CLI, portable binary, or hosted demo. An optional GFPGAN pass restores faces.
Date_Note: models published 2021–2022; repo current as reference implementation, Aug 2026
Notes: Backbone model for Upscayl and many chaiNNer graphs.

Inputs: uploaded photo; enhancement type choice
Inference_Locus: A face-restoration and unblur pipeline resolves enhanced detail from the uploaded photo per tap; facial detail is generated where the source lacks it. Runs as a hosted service on mobile and web.
Date_Note: current per vendor site, Aug 2026; vendor claims 100M monthly active users
Notes: Remini's AI Photos avatar generation set aside as image generation, out of this category.

Inputs: source image or folder; model choice (Real-ESRGAN family or converted custom models); scale
Inference_Locus: Real-ESRGAN-family models resolve upscaled output locally on a Vulkan GPU; batch mode runs a folder through the chosen model at the set scale.
Model_Backend: Real-ESRGAN via NCNN Vulkan; custom models convertible
Date_Note: v2.15 current per repo, Aug 2026

Inputs: image; scale (2x); noise level 0–3; art or photo model choice
Inference_Locus: An SRCNN-derived CNN resolves 2x upscaling and noise reduction for anime-style art, with a photo model variant; invoked per image via web demo, CLI, or third-party ports.
Model_Backend: SRCNN-inspired CNN; successor development in nunif (PyTorch)
Date_Note: original Torch7 repo superseded by nunif, Feb 2023; web demos current
Notes: Historical reference point for consumer neural upscaling, 2015 onward.

Inputs: splat file (PLY, SPZ, splat); selections, transforms, crops, color adjustments, camera animations
Inference_Locus: Selection, deletion, transform, and color edits apply directly to Gaussian primitives in the browser; no model resolves content. Runs per edit operation.
Date_Note: Open source (MIT), browser-based, local processing; PWA desktop install supported; current 2026.
Notes: The explicit row of the splat workflow: cleanup, floater removal, and publishing on primitives that a conditioned trainer produced upstream. Docs: developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/gaussian-splatting/editing/supersplat/.

Inputs: image sequence around the object, with device depth and gravity data where available; detail level setting
Inference_Locus: PhotogrammetrySession reconstructs a textured mesh from an image sequence, using depth and gravity data where the device supplies them; guided capture previews coverage on device. Runs when the session processes a reconstruction request.
Date_Note: macOS API shipped 2021 (macOS 12); on-device iOS reconstruction with guided capture shipped with iOS 17, Sept 2023.
Notes: OS-level capture API; Apple documents roughly 100 images with 70%+ overlap for reconstruction. Sample apps: developer.apple.com/documentation/RealityKit/scanning-objects-using-object-capture.

Inputs: posed images, SfM points, a designer-written training script and hyperparameters
Inference_Locus: A CUDA rasterization library optimizes Gaussian scenes from posed images under a designer-written training script; densification strategy and loss settings are addressable in code. Runs per script invocation.
Date_Note: Actively developed as of 2026; supports batch and multi-GPU rasterization, anti-aliasing, MCMC densification; backend for Splatfacto.
Notes: The code-level pipeline row: every stage of the optimization is scriptable, so specification surface is higher than the packaged trainers. Docs: docs.gsplat.studio.

Inputs: posed image set; training parameters
Inference_Locus: A hash-encoded NeRF is trained from posed images in seconds; the short loop lets the designer retrain after each capture or parameter change. Runs per training invocation with interactive rendering.
Date_Note: Code released Jan 2022; SIGGRAPH 2022 paper. Training in seconds, rendering in tens of milliseconds at 1080p per the paper.
Notes: The speedup collapsed NeRF training from hours to seconds, which changed recurrence in practice — retraining per adjustment became a working rhythm. Paper: arxiv.org/pdf/2201.05989.

Inputs: short video capture; optional 3DGS-to-Mesh toggle at upload
Inference_Locus: Splat optimization resolves a view-dependent scene from a short video capture in the cloud; an optional 3DGS-to-Mesh pass can derive a polygon mesh from the same capture. Runs per upload.
Date_Note: 3DGS scan and 3DGS-to-Mesh 2.0 documented current 2026.
Notes: Splat and mesh from one capture when the toggle is set. 3DGS-to-Mesh 2.0 showcase: kiri-innovation.github.io/3DGStoMesh2/. App also offers plain photogrammetry and LiDAR modes.

Inputs: video orbit of a low-texture, reflective, or single-colored object
Inference_Locus: Neural surface reconstruction resolves geometry from video frames for objects where photogrammetric feature matching finds few correspondences. Runs per uploaded capture.
Date_Note: NSR mode documented on vendor pages, current 2026.
Notes: A learned reconstruction stage substituting for feature matching where image evidence runs thin — more of the surface is inferred than in photo mode, hence lower x than the photogrammetry rows.

Inputs: phone video orbit of the subject or scene
Inference_Locus: Cloud processing resolves a Gaussian-splat scene from phone video, built on the prior NeRF pipeline; view-dependent appearance is fit to the capture. Runs when the capture is uploaded.

Notes: Splat files export to SIBR viewer and nerfstudio; capture development described as deprioritized in radiancefields.com/platforms/luma-ai (updated July 2026).

Inputs: images and upstream node outputs; node placement in the graph
Inference_Locus: Learned nodes resolve semantic segmentation masks and monocular depth from images inside the node graph; a Gaussian Splatting plugin can train splats from the SfM output. Runs per node execution.
Date_Note: MeshroomHub plugins (semantic segmentation, monocular depth estimation, Gaussian Splatting) shipped with 2025.1.0, Aug 2025, flagged as exploratory.
Notes: Learned stages sit as nodes in the same graph as the computational stages, so their inputs and outputs stay addressable; the models themselves resolve outside the graph's inspection.

Inputs: images plus the node graph itself: node choice, connections, per-node parameters
Inference_Locus: Each node computes one stage (feature extraction, structure-from-motion, depth maps, meshing, texturing) from the images and upstream node outputs, with parameters addressable per node in the graph. Runs when the designer executes the graph or a node.
Date_Note: 2025.1.0 released Aug 18, 2025 — restructured as a node-based visual programming toolbox; photogrammetry, camera tracking, HDR panorama, and LiDAR meshing packaged in the AliceVision plugin.
Notes: The graph makes each reconstruction stage inspectable and re-runnable — a photogrammetry pipeline with the highest explicit-specification surface in this category. Also: meshroom.org/index.php/2025/08/18/release-2025-1/.

Inputs: photo set; optionally LiDAR/laser scans, markers, masks, ground control points, per-stage parameters
Inference_Locus: Aligns photos through feature matching and bundle adjustment, then computes depth maps, point cloud or mesh, and texture from the aligned cameras; a learned model can generate masks automatically. Runs per processing stage the designer launches.
Date_Note: 2.2 (Jan 2025) added automatic AI mask generation and aerial-LiDAR boresight tools; changelog current at 2.3.1, Apr 2026 (color correction, frequency-pyramid texturing).
Notes: The AI mask generation is the documented learned stage in the 2.2.x pipeline; the 2.3.x feature list shows geometric and color processing without new learned stages. Changelog: agisoft.com/pdf/metashape_changelog.pdf.

Inputs: posed image set (COLMAP or ns-process-data); training configuration
Inference_Locus: An MLP-based radiance field is optimized from posed images; appearance between captured views is interpolated by the learned field. Runs per ns-train invocation, with a live viewer during training.
Date_Note: nerfstudio 1.0 released Jan 2024; nerfacto is the default method, described in the docs as a blend of published NeRF techniques.
Notes: Docs at docs.nerf.studio. The live viewer during training gives a mid-optimization feedback loop absent from the cloud capture services.

Inputs: posed image set with SfM seed points; training configuration
Inference_Locus: Gaussian primitives seeded from SfM points are optimized against the captured images via the gsplat rasterizer. Runs per ns-train invocation; the primitive set is exportable and editable downstream.
Date_Note: Shipped with nerfstudio 1.0, Jan 2024; Splatfacto-W variant (2024) covers unconstrained photo collections with per-image appearance embeddings.
Notes: Explicit volumetric gaussians rather than a neural field — the result stays addressable primitive-by-primitive after training, which places it slightly higher on x than nerfacto.

Inputs: photo or video capture around the subject or scene
Inference_Locus: A splat scene is optimized in the cloud from the captured frames; view-dependent appearance is fit to the capture. Runs per uploaded capture.
Date_Note: Splat capture with PLY export documented current as of 2026; results viewable in SuperSplat, Cesium, game engines.
Notes: Handles reflective and transparent material that the mesh modes drop; output is an optimized primitive set rather than a mesh.

Inputs: LiDAR sweep of the space; device camera imagery for texture
Inference_Locus: The LiDAR sensor accumulates depth into a mesh in real time during capture, fused with camera imagery for texture. Resolution happens in the sensor-fusion pipeline as the designer sweeps the space.
Date_Note: LiDAR spatial capture on iPhone Pro / iPad Pro documented current as of 2026; real-time mesh generation.
Notes: Sensed geometry rather than inferred geometry; the mesh grows live under the sweep, so what the designer covers is what resolves.

Inputs: overlapping photos taken around the subject
Inference_Locus: Cloud photogrammetry reconstructs a textured polygonal mesh from overlapping photos. Runs when the capture is uploaded for processing.
Date_Note: Object mode with photogrammetry and splat outputs documented current as of 2026; works on iOS, Android, and web without a LiDAR sensor.
Notes: Same capture flow can resolve to mesh (this row) or splats (separate row); the resolution path differs, so they sit as separate rows.

Inputs: images or video; optionally imported camera poses (COLMAP, RealityScan formats) and masks; profile and splat-count settings
Inference_Locus: Trains radiance-field scenes locally from images or video, importing camera poses where supplied; training renders live and can be stopped, resumed, and cropped. Runs per training session on the designer's GPU.
Date_Note: Open beta from late 2023; 1.0 out of beta Aug 2025; 1.1.x adds SPZ v4 and HTML export targets.
Notes: Local desktop training with live view — the designer watches the optimization and intervenes, in contrast with the upload-and-wait capture services. Platform page: radiancefields.com/platforms/postshot.

Inputs: photo set; optionally laser scans, aerial LiDAR, control points, region boxes, reconstruction settings
Inference_Locus: Camera poses, depth maps, mesh, and texture are computed from the photo set through feature matching, bundle adjustment, and multi-view stereo; a learned model can generate subject masks before alignment. Runs when the designer starts an alignment or reconstruction step.
Date_Note: RealityCapture rebranded RealityScan 2.0 June 2025 (AI mask generation, aerial LiDAR); 2.1 Nov 2025 added CLI docs and gRPC/REST headless service; 2.2 June 24, 2026 added 360 workflow and AMD GPU support.
Notes: SfM and MVS stages resolve geometrically from image evidence; the mask generation added in 2.0 is a learned stage inside an otherwise computational pipeline. Camera registrations feed splat trainers (Postshot, gsplat pipelines) downstream. Coverage: cgchannel.com/2025/06/epic-games-to-rebrand-realitycapture-as-realityscan-2-0, radiancefields.com/realityscan-2.2-adds-360-and-amd-gpu-support.
